newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe stresses Europe, gradual reform in programme.
newsitem.headline: Juppe stresses Europe, gradual reform in programme.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe outlined his centre-right coalition's programme for an early parliamentary election on Tuesday, stressing his commitment to Europe and to gradual, market-oriented economic reforms.

Seeking to unite the sometimes fractious alliance, Juppe praised the achievements of his conservative predecessor Edouard Balladur, who ran unsuccessfully against fellow Gaullist Jacques Chirac in a 1995 presidential election, splitting the Right.

The prime minister said he planned to run the campaign for the May 25-June 1 election on his vision of France's future rather than on his record, which has featured a relentless rise in unemployment to a record 12.8 percent.
"We have laid the basis for the revival of our country after years of decline. We have taken difficult and courageous decisions. We have begun to adapt France to its times," he said.

Juppe proposed what he called a new contract for the year 2000 based on four major objectives: "Building a modern state, freeing business and the spirit of enterprise to create the jobs we need, renovating the French social and cultural model, making the big Europe a success at last."

He began his keynote address to an invited audience of outgoing Gaullist and centre-right UDF parliamentarians 20 minutes late in a Paris congress centre beneath the giant slogan "With Jacques Chirac, a new impulse for France."
